answer: Bonded identity staking blunts Sybil attacks: every agent locks collateral before its vote counts, and the chain records each bond in a public atlas of identities. An attacker cannot mint hollow accounts for free - each fake persona needs its own stake, slashed the moment linked wallets coordinate to double-vote or forge work. Even hiding behind a plume of shells, shared funding shows up in the atlas, so it still pays the whole bond up front and forfeits it all on detection. Cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, making large attacks prohibitively expensive.
